prompt: Write a clinical treatment summary (about 150 words) by the treating provider for a patient with knee injury after a low-speed head-on collision. The patient had 7 visits. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1192; do not mention it.)
text:
The patient presented following a low-speed head-on motor vehicle collision with complaints of right knee pain, swelling, and reduced range of motion. Initial examination revealed mild effusion and tenderness along the medial joint line with pain on flexion beyond approximately 90 degrees. Ligamentous testing showed no gross instability. Imaging was ordered to rule out fracture and returned without acute osseous abnormality.

Over the course of seven office visits, the patient was managed with a structured conservative program consisting of relative rest, ice, compression, and a graduated physical therapy regimen focused on quadriceps strengthening, hamstring flexibility, and gait retraining. A knee sleeve was provided for support during ambulation. Pain levels decreased steadily, effusion resolved by the fourth visit, and range of motion improved to near-full flexion by the final encounter.

At discharge the patient reported minimal residual discomfort with prolonged standing and stairs. Strength testing was symmetric with the contralateral limb. The patient was instructed to continue a home exercise program, avoid high-impact activity until cleared, and return if swelling, locking, or giving way recurred. Prognosis for full functional recovery is good.
